title: Sun and moon at Gettysburg, June 25 to July 7, 1863
status: Computed (not measured). The clock this is tied to (local mean time) is a convention of this project, not a record of any 1863 clock.

site.name: Gettysburg, Pennsylvania (nominal point)
site.note: Sea-level observer, the USNO default. The town is about 150 m above sea level; a real horizon (the ridges, Seminary Ridge and the Round Tops) would change rise and set times by minutes and is not modelled.

time_conventions.lmt_definition: Local mean time at the site longitude: LMT = UT + longitude_east / 15 h. At 77.2311 W that is UT - 5 h 8.92 min.
time_conventions.no_standard_time_1863: There was no standard time in 1863. Towns set clocks to local mean solar time or to a railway's own time; US standard time zones came with the railroads on 18 November 1883 (source wikipedia-time-us). LMT is therefore a convention, and the EST-equivalent column is offered because modern almanacs (USNO tz=-5) and the pitch quote it.
time_conventions.day_boundaries: A day is a local-mean-time calendar day [00:00, 24:00) LMT. An event can fall on a different EST-equivalent date (field est_date).
time_conventions.rounding: hh:mm values are rounded to the nearest minute (half up); lmt_hms shows seconds as computed. Real accuracy is about +-1 minute (ephemeris and refraction model), so no claim finer than one minute is made.
time_conventions.tick_clock: The 675-tick clock is a CANDIDATE (data-src/time/time_anchors.json, version 2026-09-30.1, release "candidate"; five anchors await a historian). astro_by_day.json does not depend on it. astro_by_tick.json depends on it only through tools/environment/tickclock.mjs tickToLmtMinutes() and embeds the anchors it used.

definitions.sunrise_sunset: Upper limb of the sun on the horizon, with 34 arcmin of standard atmospheric refraction, observer at sea level.
definitions.civil_twilight: Centre of the sun 6 degrees below the horizon (civil_dawn, civil_dusk). Nautical: 12 degrees. (USNO's one-day API lists civil twilight only, so nautical times are cross-checked by methods A and B only.)
definitions.moonrise_moonset: Upper limb of the moon on the horizon, topocentric, 34 arcmin standard refraction.
definitions.transit: Upper transit: the body crosses the local meridian.
definitions.illumination: Illuminated fraction of the lunar disc, in percent, at 12:00 LMT (illumination_noon_lmt_pct) and at 12:00 EST-equivalent (illumination_noon_est_pct, the instant at which USNO's integer percentage was found to agree).
definitions.phase_name: Name of the principal phase (New Moon, First Quarter, Full Moon, Last Quarter) if that phase falls inside the local-mean-time calendar day; otherwise the octant of the moon's ecliptic elongation at 12:00 LMT (0-90 Waxing Crescent, 90-180 Waxing Gibbous, 180-270 Waning Gibbous, 270-360 Waning Crescent). USNO instead names the state at noon, so labels can differ on a quarter-phase day (the numbers do not).

sources.title: Astronomy Engine 2.1.19 (Don Cross), MIT licence
sources.note: Sun/Moon positions, SearchRiseSet (upper limb, standard refraction), SearchAltitude, SearchHourAngle, SearchMoonQuarter, Illumination, MoonPhase. Used as the primary generator.

sources.title: tools/environment/solar.mjs: dependency-free implementation of J. Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms (2nd ed., 1998) ch. 10, 12, 22, 25, 40, 47 (truncated), 48
sources.note: Independent second implementation; shares no code or tables with astronomy-engine. Moon series truncated to the largest terms (about 0.02 degree).

sources.title: U.S. Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications Department, Complete Sun and Moon Data for One Day (API v4.0.1, endpoint rstt/oneday)
sources.note: US Government work (public domain). Returns whole minutes only; tz must be a multiple of 0.25 h, so tz=-5 (EST-equivalent) was requested and local mean time derived. One request per day, cached; never called from visitors' browsers.

sources.title: Fred Espenak, NASA/GSFC, Phases of the Moon: 1801 to 1900 (Universal Time)
sources.note: Principal phases to the minute in UT. NASA credit line: Fred Espenak, NASA/GSFC (eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov).

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Time in the United States" (CC BY-SA 4.0)
sources.note: Background only: before November 18, 1883 many towns set clocks to local mean solar time; four standard time zones were introduced by the railroads on that date.

methods.name: astronomy-engine
methods.note: Sun and Moon topocentric positions with aberration and nutation, observer at sea level (0 m), rise/set of the upper limb with 34 arcmin standard refraction.

methods.name: tools/environment/solar.mjs
methods.role: independent deterministic re-computation (Meeus), compared on every value

methods.name: USNO AA API rstt/oneday v4.0.1, tz=-5
NASA/GSFC Espenak phases1801.html
methods.role: authority cross-check of principal phases (UT, whole minutes)

badge_legend.Computed: derived from an ephemeris, not observed
badge_legend.Measured: an instrument reading (none in this file)
badge_legend.Modelled: an estimate from a model (none in this file)

usno.note: diff = astronomy-engine minus USNO, in minutes, where USNO lists whole minutes (so a diff up to +-0.5 is rounding).
usno.illumination_note: USNO lists an integer percentage; ours at 12:00 EST-equivalent (2 decimals) is compared after rounding to an integer, and the largest unrounded difference is given in max_abs_illumination_diff_pct.
phase_label_disagreements: 1863-07-07: ours Last Quarter, USNO Waning Gibbous

nasa.note: NASA lists UT to the minute and appears to truncate seconds (every astronomy-engine minus NASA difference falls in [0, 1) minute), so a difference under one minute is rounding, not disagreement.
